LESSON: RHYTHM COMPOSING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: CREATING/
Topic 2.1: Rhythm COMPOSING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Rhythm COMPOSING. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. clap/tap/stamp/vocalise guided to clap/vocalise the rhythms of rhythms of names and sounds from the environment for rhythm articulation,
2. identify repetition and variations to rhythms in familiar tunes in order to use the technique in varying other tunes and own composition,
3. create simple rhythmic accompaniments to songs and stories/poems/rhymes using animals/birds in the environment such as voice, body percussions or the cuckoo, donkey and crested crane. improvised percussion instruments as a basis of compositional skills, e) record and playback constant rhythmic sounds from the environment on a digital device for digital literacy. are rhythmical by tapping/clapping in accompaniment to simple songs and stories constant rhythmic sounds from the environment on digital devices

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Rhythm COMPOSING.
2. Explain Rhythm COMPOSING to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Rhythm COMPOSING.
4. Show that you can: clap/tap/stamp/vocalise guided to clap/vocalise the rhythms of rhythms of names and sounds from the environment for rhythm articulation,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Rhythm COMPOSING. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Rhythm COMPOSING important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. clap/tap/stamp/vocalise guided to clap/vocalise the rhythms of rhythms of names and sounds from the environment for rhythm articulation,
2. identify repetition and variations to rhythms in familiar tunes in order to use the technique in varying other tunes and own composition,
3. create simple rhythmic accompaniments to songs and stories/poems/rhymes using animals/birds in the environment such as voice, body percussions or the cuckoo, donkey and crested crane. improvised percussion instruments as a basis of compositional skills, e) record and playback constant rhythmic sounds from the environment on a digital device for digital literacy. are rhythmical by tapping/clapping in accompaniment to simple songs and stories constant rhythmic sounds from the environment on digital devices
